cleanIntro:
The VICTRA-20 is YHM's modular 20 gauge shotgun can. It mounts on the shotgun's own choke threads, and it comes apart: an endcap held by Allen bolts, baffles in pairs on two threaded rods, and a blast chamber. Run it full length at 10 inches, or with YHM's shorter rod kits at 8, 6 or 4 inches.

YHM publishes the owner's teardown, and the cleaning needs it. The job is plastic wad debris on the baffles and the rods. The rods may soak overnight in wad solvent; the aluminium baffles must never soak in any solvent. YHM's interval is at least every 500 rounds.

This guide follows YHM's own VICTRA-20 user manual (part number YHM-1300). That book names the VICTRA-20. It does not print the word "Modular" in the name.

steps.title: Shotgun unloaded, muzzle somewhere safe
steps.action: Before the can or its mount is touched, unload the host shotgun by its own manual and keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction. YHM puts this before both fitting and removal. The book covers the suppressor only; how to unload your shotgun is in that shotgun's manual.
steps.quote: Be certain the firearm is unloaded and the muzzle is pointed in a safe direction before starting this installation and removal process.
steps.cite: YHM VICTRA™-20 Suppressor user manual, part number YHM-1300 — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "052026", unlabelled — INSTALLATION AND USE, PDF p.5

steps.title: Let it cool before you touch it
steps.action: A shotgun can gets very hot. Leave it where it is, away from anything that could melt or catch fire, until it has cooled. Then take hold of it.
steps.quote: Do not attempt to touch or remove the sound suppressor until it has cooled.
steps.cite: YHM VICTRA™-20 Suppressor user manual, part number YHM-1300 — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "052026", unlabelled — VICTRA - 20 CARE, PDF p.3
steps.warn: Caution! The sound suppressor can become extremely hot after discharging your firearm!

steps.title: Can off the shotgun as soon as you finish shooting
steps.action: Take the can off the gun at the end of the session. Moisture trapped inside causes corrosion, and taking the can off lets it dry out. The can unscrews from the mount, and the mount stays in the choke threads. YHM prints the fitting order (mount, jam nut, can) but no removal sequence, so this guide does not write one. With the can off, put a thread protector on the mount.
steps.aside: YHM recommends using a thread protector* to protect the mount threads during storage
steps.quote: The best way to prevent corrosion of your firearm is to remove the suppressor as soon as you are finished shooting.
steps.cite: YHM VICTRA™-20 Suppressor user manual, part number YHM-1300 — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "052026", unlabelled — VICTRA - 20 CARE, PDF p.3

steps.title: Stand it on a mat, blast chamber end down
steps.action: Stand the can on a gun mat with the blast chamber end down, the end that went against the mount. The endcap with the Allen bolts now faces up. The mat protects the anodized finish.
steps.quote: To disassemble your suppressor, place the suppressor, blast chamber end down, on your gun mat
steps.cite: YHM VICTRA™-20 Suppressor user manual, part number YHM-1300 — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "052026", unlabelled — DISASSEMBLING THE VICTRA-20, PDF p.8

steps.title: Allen nuts off the face with a 5/32 inch Allen wrench
steps.action: Loosen and remove the Allen nuts on the face of the can with a 5/32 inch Allen wrench. YHM does not supply this wrench. Put the nuts somewhere they cannot roll away, because the endcap cannot be secured without them.
steps.aside: Set them aside in a safe place.
steps.quote: Use your 5/32” Allen wrench (not provided) and loosen, then remove the Allen nuts on the face of the suppressor.
steps.cite: YHM VICTRA™-20 Suppressor user manual, part number YHM-1300 — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "052026", unlabelled — DISASSEMBLING THE VICTRA-20, PDF p.8

steps.title: Endcap up off the rods, then the baffles
steps.action: Hold the base of the can and lift the endcap up off the assembly rods. Then lift the baffles off the rods. They come off in pairs, and the endcap still holds the choke. Keep the baffles in the order they came off.
steps.quote: Hold the base of your suppressor and begin removing the endcap off the assembly rods.
steps.cite: YHM VICTRA™-20 Suppressor user manual, part number YHM-1300 — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "052026", unlabelled — DISASSEMBLING THE VICTRA-20, PDF p.8

steps.title: Rods out of the blast chamber
steps.action: With only the blast chamber and the two rods left, unscrew the rods out of the blast chamber. That is as far as YHM takes the can apart.
steps.quote: When you have only the blast chamber and rods left, unscrew the rods out from the blast chamber.
steps.cite: YHM VICTRA™-20 Suppressor user manual, part number YHM-1300 — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "052026", unlabelled — DISASSEMBLING THE VICTRA-20, PDF p.8

steps.title: Field strip complete: blast chamber, rods, baffles, endcap
steps.action: The can is off the gun and in its parts: blast chamber, two assembly rods, baffle pairs, and the endcap with its choke and Allen nuts. Deep Clean has YHM's published cleaning, the reassembly with its torque, the shorter configurations and the choke change.
steps.prose: YHM sets a minimum interval, not a fixed one. Ammunition, the host gun, rain and humidity all shorten it.
steps.quote: We recommend cleaning the sound suppressor at minimum after every 500 rounds.
steps.cite: YHM VICTRA™-20 Suppressor user manual, part number YHM-1300 — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "052026", unlabelled — VICTRA - 20 CARE, PDF p.3

deepSteps.title: Pick the mating surfaces of the baffles clean
deepSteps.action: Plastic from the wads builds up on the baffles and interrupters, and it has to come off. Go round the faces where each baffle meets the next with a pick or a similar tool until no debris is left. Debris left on a mating face stops the stack seating flat.
deepSteps.quote: are clean by using a pick or similar tool to remove any debris.
deepSteps.cite: YHM VICTRA™-20 Suppressor user manual, part number YHM-1300 — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "052026", unlabelled — CLEANING & MAINTENANCE, PDF p.12

deepSteps.title: Solvent label read, ventilation, skin and eye protection
deepSteps.action: Before the wad solvent comes out, read the warning label on it. Work somewhere with good air flow, and wear gloves and eye protection.
deepSteps.quote: Always use adequate ventilation and wear both skin and eye protection when using solvents.
deepSteps.cite: YHM VICTRA™-20 Suppressor user manual, part number YHM-1300 — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "052026", unlabelled — CLEANING & MAINTENANCE, CAUTION, PDF p.12

deepSteps.title: Rods only: soak overnight in shotgun wad solvent
deepSteps.action: Soak the two assembly rods overnight in a shotgun-specific cleaning solution. YHM names Brownells Shotgun Wad Solvent as an example. The soak loosens the plastic so it comes off. Only the rods go in the soak.
deepSteps.quote: (such as Brownells® Shotgun Wad Solvent) should loosen and remove plastic debris without issue.
deepSteps.cite: YHM VICTRA™-20 Suppressor user manual, part number YHM-1300 — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "052026", unlabelled — CLEANING & MAINTENANCE, PDF p.12

deepSteps.title: Baffles: soapy water and a brush, never a soak
deepSteps.action: The baffles are aluminium. Never soak them in any solvent, the wad solvent included, because solvent can damage the finish. Wipe them with a cloth and soapy water, or scrub them gently with a brush.
deepSteps.aside: we recommend using a cloth with soapy water or a brush to gently wipe or scrub away debris.
deepSteps.quote: should NOT be soaked in ANY solvent
deepSteps.cite: YHM VICTRA™-20 Suppressor user manual, part number YHM-1300 — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "052026", unlabelled — CLEANING & MAINTENANCE, NOTE, PDF p.12

deepSteps.title: Rods into the blast chamber until they bottom out
deepSteps.action: Lay the blast chamber on the mat and screw the two rods in until they bottom out. For a shorter can, use two rods of the same length for the length you want: 8, 6 or 4 inch. YHM sells these rod kits separately.
deepSteps.aside: Place blast chamber on your gun mat.
deepSteps.quote: Thread rods into blast chamber until they bottom-out,
deepSteps.cite: YHM VICTRA™-20 Suppressor user manual, part number YHM-1300 — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "052026", unlabelled — REASSEMBLING THE VICTRA-20, PDF p.9

deepSteps.title: Baffles back on in pairs, long one first
deepSteps.action: Slide the baffles back onto the rods in pairs: a long baffle, then a short one, and repeat until the can is the length you want. A long baffle always sits next to the blast chamber. For a shorter can, leave pairs off the front: one pair for 8 inches, two for 6, three for 4. The reassembly page calls the pair a guide baffle and an interrupter baffle; the modularity page calls them long and short.
deepSteps.aside: Remove 1 pair for 8” assembly and remove 2 pairs for 6” assembly.
deepSteps.quote: Always ensure there is a long baffle adjacent to the blast chamber, regardless of configuration.
deepSteps.cite: YHM VICTRA™-20 Suppressor user manual, part number YHM-1300 — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "052026", unlabelled — VICTRA-20 MODULARITY, PDF p.10

deepSteps.title: Choke change, in the endcap
deepSteps.action: The choke threads into the endcap. To change it, take the installed choke out of the endcap with the supplied wrench, put in the choke you want, and tighten it with the same wrench. YHM lists Improved Cylinder (in the box), Modified and Full.
deepSteps.aside: Tighten the choke to the endcap using the wrench.
deepSteps.quote: remove the installed choke from the endcap using the supplied wrench and replace with the desired choke.
deepSteps.cite: YHM VICTRA™-20 Suppressor user manual, part number YHM-1300 — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "052026", unlabelled — VICTRA-20 MODULARITY, PDF p.10
deepSteps.warn: High-density shot such as Hevi-Shot, Federal TSS, or similar tungsten or bismuth loads, as well as slugs, are not to be used with a full choke.

deepSteps.title: Endcap over the rods, Allen bolts to 40-45 in-lb
deepSteps.action: Slide the endcap, with its choke fitted, down over the rods. Secure it with the Allen bolts and a 5/32 inch Allen wrench, torqued to 40 to 45 inch-pounds. Inch-pounds, not foot-pounds: use an inch-pound torque driver.
deepSteps.quote: Slip the endcap, over the rods and secure the Allen head bolts with a 5/32” Allen wrench.
deepSteps.cite: YHM VICTRA™-20 Suppressor user manual, part number YHM-1300 — UNKNOWN — no revision or document number is printed; the last page carries only "052026", unlabelled — REASSEMBLING THE VICTRA-20, PDF p.9

cleaning.name: OUTSIDE OF THE CAN
tasks: Can cool before it is touched
Excess oil, dirt and other contaminants wiped off the outside with a cloth dipped in mild gun cleaning solvent
Off the gun as soon as shooting is done, so the inside can dry

cleaning.name: BAFFLES AND INTERRUPTERS
tasks: Plastic wad debris removed from every baffle and interrupter
Mating surfaces picked clean with a pick or a similar tool
Wiped with a cloth and soapy water, or gently scrubbed with a brush
⛔ Never soak the aluminium baffles in any solvent

cleaning.name: ASSEMBLY RODS
tasks: Rods soaked overnight in a shotgun-specific wad solvent to loosen the plastic
⚠ Read the solvent's warning label; ventilation, skin and eye protection

cleaning.name: BACK TOGETHER
tasks: Rods threaded into the blast chamber until they bottom out, both the same length
Baffles in pairs, a long baffle always next to the blast chamber
Endcap Allen bolts torqued to 40-45 in-lb with a 5/32 inch Allen wrench

cleaning.name: ⛔ WHAT NEVER GOES THROUGH IT
tasks: ⛔ Never fire it with water or any other media inside
⛔ Do not shoot through an obstructed suppressor; a can that has been in water is drained completely first
⛔ Do not use Flitecontrol or similar wads
⛔ Do not use high-density shot or slugs through a full choke
Single-barrel shotguns only, factory-loaded ammunition only, shell length within the barrel-length table

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: If it stays on the gun, store the gun muzzle-down with the action open
Thread protector on the mount when the can is off

reassembly: Can rebuilt and torqued: rods bottomed out in the blast chamber, baffles in pairs with a long baffle next to the blast chamber, choke tight in the endcap, endcap Allen bolts at 40-45 in-lb.
Shotgun unloaded and the muzzle pointed in a safe direction before the mount or the can goes on.

Mount screwed into the barrel's choke threads with the spanner wrench supplied with the can. The VICTRA-20 and the 12 gauge Victra-12 have different thread pitches, so this can does not go on a 12 gauge gun.
Jam nut run back against the shoulder of the mount, then the can threaded on until it stops.
Can backed off no more than one turn, until the index notch on the blast chamber lines up with the front sight bead.
Jam nut tightened with the supplied wrench until it is firmly against the can.
fncheck: With the shotgun unloaded, check the fit before firing. The threaded mount is fully screwed into the barrel, the can is tight on the mount, and the jam nut is firmly against the can with the index notch on the front bead. Look through the can: nothing may be inside it, and a can that has been in water, even briefly, is fully drained first. Check the barrel length against the shell: a 7.5 inch or longer barrel for 2¾ inch shells, 10 inches or longer for 3 inch, 16 inches or longer for 3½ inch. While shooting, check often that the mount is still tight in the barrel and the can is still tight on the mount. YHM lists the can coming loose from the gun as the first common cause of a baffle strike.
